text:
tara: Hey team, getting repeated 401 invalid_api_key when using the temp dev key from the dashboard on my devbox. Worked earlier today, now failing. curl output below.

kevin: Can you paste the curl + response? Also which org/project and whether it's hosted vs dedicated?

tara: curl command:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Api-Key ______" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": "invalid_api_key",
  "message": "Key expired",
  "code": 401
}
```

kevin: That looks like an expired TTL temp key. Did you create it via `redwood keys create --ttl` or from dashboard?

tara: created via dashboard -> Dev keys -> Create temporary, TTL 1h, got string, exported into `REDWOOD_API_KEY` in my .bashrc. I did `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY | tail -c 8` returns `...9a7f2b`.

sam: Quick sanity check: make sure header scheme is `Api-Key` not `Bearer`. Also confirm no extra newlines -- `printf '%s' "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | wc -c` should match length 40.

tara: ran length check: 44 chars. hmmm.

kevin: That suggests maybe dashboard applied rotation/policy or it was revoked. Can you confirm key id shown in dashboard matches key last-8? Also check org-level SSO policy: sometimes temp keys auto-revoke on SSO rebind.

tara: Dashboard shows key id `dev-temp-2026-03-05` and status 'active'. No recent SSO events.

eng-oncall: possibility: if you're using a private/delegated org, temp keys may be scoped to Hosted vs Dedicated. Try hitting `https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/verify` with the key to get details.

tara: ran verify:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Api-Key $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/verify
```
Resp: 401 same payload.

support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-21568 linking thread (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-21568)

kevin: Okay, we'll repro. In meantime, generate a new temp key via CLI and try:
```
redwood keys create --name devbox-temp --ttl 3600 --json | jq -r .key > /tmp/rk
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat /tmp/rk)
printf '%s' "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | wc -c
curl -H "Authorization: Api-Key $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models
```

sam: Also check if your devbox clock is >5min off — JWT-ish time checks can cause invalidation for short TTL keys.

tara: ran CLI flow, new key length 40, verify endpoint returns 200 and key metadata. Calls to embeddings now succeed.

kevin: Thanks — sounds like the dashboard-created key got auto-revoked (we'll investigate rotations). Leaving ticket for backend team to check revocation logs. :thumbsup: 

tara: Thanks all. FYI I'll add automated CLI key creation to my devbox startup script to avoid repeats. :white_check_mark:

eng-oncall: logged follow-up for infra team: INFRA-4921 (check dashboard temp key lifecycle).
